Read a matrix of numbers from text, one row per line, and answer any row or column.

Adapted from Exercism's [problem specification](https://github.com/exercism/problem-specifications/tree/main/exercises/matrix) (MIT). Listed under [Grids & Matrices](/examples/?subject=grids-and-matrices).

```nomi-run
// FILE: matrix.nomi
//# A matrix read from text, and its rows and columns.

/// A matrix of numbers read from text, one row per line.
pub opaque struct Matrix {
    rows: Vector<Vector<Int>>
}

/// Why text is not a matrix.
pub enum Error {
    NotANumber String
}

impl Matrix {
    /// The matrix whose rows are the lines of `text`, each a list of numbers
    /// separated by spaces, or `NotANumber` with the first word that is not
    /// one.
    pub fn parse(text: String) -> Result<Matrix, Error> {
        rows =
            text
            |> String.lines()
            |> Iter.map(parse_row)
            |> Result.collect()?

        Ok(#Matrix{rows: Iter.to_vector(rows)})
    }

    /// The numbers of row `index`, counted from 1, or `None` past the last.
    pub fn row(matrix: Matrix, index: Int) -> Maybe<List<Int>> {
        matrix.rows
        |> Vector.get(index - 1)?
        |> Iter.to_list()
        |> Some()
    }

    /// The numbers of column `index`, counted from 1, top to bottom, or
    /// `None` past the last.
    pub fn column(matrix: Matrix, index: Int) -> Maybe<List<Int>> {
        matrix.rows
        |> Iter.map(&Vector.get(&1, index - 1))
        |> Maybe.collect()
    }
}

fn parse_row(line: String) -> Result<Vector<Int>, Error> {
    line
    |> String.words()
    |> Iter.map(fn word -> String.to_int(word) |> Maybe.to_result(Error.NotANumber(word)))
    |> Result.collect()?
    |> Iter.to_vector()
    |> Ok()
}

// FILE: matrix_test.nomi
import matrix.{Error, Matrix}

test "rows" {
    cases = [
        #("extract row from one number matrix", "1", 1, [1]),
        #("can extract row", "1 2\n3 4", 2, [3, 4]),
        #("extract row where numbers have different widths", "1 2\n10 20", 2, [10, 20]),
        #(
            "can extract row from non-square matrix with no corresponding column",
            "1 2 3\n4 5 6\n7 8 9\n8 7 6",
            4,
            [8, 7, 6],
        ),
    ]

    subtests cases, #(description, text, index, expected), description {
        assert Ok(matrix) = Matrix.parse(text)

        assert Matrix.row(matrix, index) == Some(expected)
    }
}

test "columns" {
    cases = [
        #("extract column from one number matrix", "1", 1, [1]),
        #("can extract column", "1 2 3\n4 5 6\n7 8 9", 3, [3, 6, 9]),
        #(
            "can extract column from non-square matrix with no corresponding row",
            "1 2 3 4\n5 6 7 8\n9 8 7 6",
            4,
            [4, 8, 6],
        ),
        #(
            "extract column where numbers have different widths",
            "89 1903 3\n18 3 1\n9 4 800",
            2,
            [1903, 3, 4],
        ),
    ]

    subtests cases, #(description, text, index, expected), description {
        assert Ok(matrix) = Matrix.parse(text)

        assert Matrix.column(matrix, index) == Some(expected)
    }
}

// Not canonical: the canonical matrices are all well formed and every index
// is in range.
test "a word that is not a number is an error" {
    assert Matrix.parse("1 2\n3 four") == Err(Error.NotANumber("four"))
}

test "an index past the last row or column is None" {
    matrix = Matrix.parse("1 2\n3 4")?

    assert Matrix.row(matrix, 3) == None
    assert Matrix.column(matrix, 0) == None
}
```

## How it's written

- `Matrix.parse` reads the text once into an opaque struct of a `Vector<Vector<Int>>`, so `row` and `column` index it and never parse again. Each line is split with `String.words`, which ignores the different widths of the numbers.
- A word that is not a number is `Err(Error.NotANumber(word))`, through `Maybe.to_result` per word and `Result.collect()?` per row and over the rows. `row` is `Vector.get(index - 1)?` as one stage of a pipe. The canonical data has no such case; the test file adds one, marked not canonical.
- `row` and `column` count from 1, as the canonical data does, and answer `Maybe<List<Int>>`: an index past the last row or column is `None`, which the test file also checks outside the canonical cases. `column` is `Vector.get` on every row, gathered with `Maybe.collect`, so it is `None` if any row is too short.
- The row and column groups are one `subtests` table each, named by the description column. A row's body takes the matrix apart with `assert Ok(matrix) = Matrix.parse(text)`, since a `?` cannot leave a `subtests` row.
